#3576. James Gunn’s Exit from DC Studios Was Due to Tensions with Skydance's Executives, Report Says

It’s been just over four years since James Gunn and Peter Safran took the reins at DC Studios as co-CEOs. For fans impressed by Gunn’s Marvel films, including Guardians of the Galaxy, the prospect of what Gunn and Safran could bring to DC comics adaptations across film, animation, and television was especially exciting.

However, Gunn and Safran’s full vision may never reach fruition, and now, thanks to The Hollywood Reporter, we have a plausible explanation.

Soon after Skydance acquired Warner Bros. Discovery, major changes swept through Warner Bros., including a restructuring and layoffs. Warner Bros. heads Pam Abdy and Mike De Luca were also let go. Gunn and Safran were believed to have escaped such a fate. That was the case, at least until Skydance co-CEOs David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz arrived at Gunn and Safran’s offices on the Warner Bros. lot on Nov. 6, marking a turning point for DC Studios.

According to The Hollywood Reporter’s sources, Gunn and Safran were told that, despite being previously reassured their roles would be safe under the new merger, Skydance’s co-CEOs had changed their minds. Though Gunn and Safran are no longer CEOs of DC Studios, Warner Bros. Discovery did announce that the two will “ensure a smooth, collaborative transition” of the studio to new leadership: Jeremy Latcham, previously a key member of Marvel Studios’ executive team.

The Hollywood Reporter's insider revealed that Latcham’s move into Gunn and Safran’s role had been in the works since early fall, when Skydance Motion Picture Group co-chairs Josh Greenstein and Dana Goldberg approached him. The situation is particularly damning because other sources point to “several points of tension” between Greenstein and Goldberg and Gunn and Safran. Before the merger, Gunn and Safran reported directly to Warner Bros. CEO David Zaslav and had tight control over DC’s product rollout, spanning movies, TV shows, and animation.

Reportedly, this didn’t work particularly well for Greenstein and Goldberg, who were trying to consolidate all motion pictures under their leadership. Furthermore, Gunn and Safran were reportedly “too slow” to share plans, details, or even footage with Skydance’s leadership.

The Hollywood Reporter also mentions that Skydance's new leadership wasn't partiuclarly impressed with the results achieved by DC Studios under Gunn and Safran's guidance. Their most successful movie, Superman, which grossed $618 million, "did not net out," according to The Hollywood Reporter, and failed to achieve the kind of pop culture impact the executives expected. While Clayface grossed over $100 million on a relatively small budget, Supergirl was "a disaster in the eyes of the new regime," The Hollywood Reporter's sources say.

The main reason Gunn and Safran’s vision for DC Studios failed will be debated for years. For now, though, the answer seems to be studio politics and business results. It’s a sad end to their leadership, but one that, if box-office numbers are any indication, we ultimately saw coming.

#3575. Why Those Flashy Halloween Contacts Are a Bad Idea

Contacts with cat pupils or neon colors can be fun, but are you sure you want to put a piece of plastic from a costume store into your eye? Experts, like those at the American Academy of Ophthalmology, warn against it. These non-prescription contacts are technically illegal in the U.S. (even though plenty of companies sell them anyway). The CDC warns that the risks include "eye sores and vision loss."

Cheap Halloween contacts tend to be one-size-fits-all, but the AAO points out that contacts should never be one-size-fits-all. A contact that is too large or too small for your eye can cause corneal abrasions, corneal ulcers, and can result in infections like keratitis. Infections can, in severe cases, lead to blindness. A 2017 report from the FDA found bacterial contamination in 27% of costume contacts.

If you do wear contacts (Halloween or otherwise), the AAO recommends keeping an eye out for symptoms like redness, swelling, pain, or excessive discharge. Seek care as soon as you suspect an infection. Your eyes are more sensitive to infections than other parts of the body, so be cautious.

Legally, contacts require a prescription, so if those colored contacts you're eyeing can be bought without showing a doctor’s prescription, they’re not legit. The real thing can be expensive, though: I found prices of $40 and up from lens.com, Discount Contacts, and Wicked Eyez.

These websites all let you order online, but you’ll have to provide your prescription information before you can check out. Fortunately, the Federal Trade Commission has ruled that providers must give you your contact prescription after a fitting so that you can take the prescription elsewhere. And they cannot charge you extra for this.

Once you’ve got the lenses, you have to know how to take care of them. If you wear contacts every day, you already know the drill. But if you’re just picking up a pair to use with a costume, here are the basics:

Wash your hands before handling the lenses.

Store them in contact lens solution, and keep the lenses and their case clean.

And for Pete’s sake, don’t share them with your friends!

Just remember, the bloodshot look stops being cool after you take your zombie costume off.

#3574. This Classic Marvel Villain Could Reshape The MCU — And Introduce Nova

With heavy-hitting villains like Loki, Thanos, the Red Skull, Galactus, and now Doctor Doom already featured — and in most cases, thoroughly defeated — in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, it's easy to wonder who might be next in line to pose a threat to the Avengers. It is, after all, pretty difficult to raise the stakes higher than the death and resurrection of half the universe in "Infinity War" and "Endgame," even when there's an entire multiverse out there just waiting to be put in danger. There is, however, one major Marvel Comics villain who has yet to step into the spotlight in the movies, with a track record as one of the deadliest enemies not just to a single team of heroes, but to the entire cosmos.

Annihilus, the insectoid ruler of the Negative Zone, has over 60 years of comics history and has proven himself to be every bit as deadly as Thanos, but without the veneer of nobility that came with the goal of seeking some kind of cosmic balance. Annihilus has no noble goals or grand designs, just a massive army of mindless drones hellbent on consuming everything in its path, and if he's introduced into the MCU, he has the potential to not only wreak havoc across the entire universe, but also pave the way to finally introduce the fan-favorite hero Nova to the big screen.

Originally introduced in 1968's "Fantastic Four Annual" #6 with the ominously over-the-top nickname of "The Living Death That Walks," Annihilus was at one point considered by director James Gunn to be the villain of "Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3," and with good reason. While he's been a perennial foe for the Fantastic Four, Annihilus' most prominent and destructive moments came in the 2006 crossover "Annihilation," which saw him unleash billions of locust-like drones across the galaxy in an "Annihilation Wave" that toppled long-established star-spanning empires and still has lasting effects on the Marvel Universe two real-time decades later.

Perhaps most importantly, "Annihilation" paved the way for the introduction of the modern Guardians of the Galaxy. Rather than the original Guardians concept of a team of sci-fi heroes in the distant future of the 30th century, Annihilation and its sequel, "Annihilation Conquest," rebooted them as space-faring hard-luck heroes led by Star-Lord, which led directly to the version that made it to the MCU. As a result, Annihilus is a natural fit to face off against the Guardians in some form, so it makes sense that he'd be considered for the third film, even if the decision was ultimately made to focus more on Rocket's origin and pit the heroes against the High Evolutionary instead.

Despite not making it into "Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3," Annihilus remains one of the biggest comic book supervillains who hasn't been tapped for a role in the movies, providing the MCU with an opportunity — although not necessarily one that fans might expect. After "Annihilation," Annihilus wasn't just tied to the Fantastic Four, but found a new arch-enemy: Nova.

The Nova Corps were introduced to the MCU back in the first "Guardians" movie as an organization of galactic peacekeepers, but Earth's representative, Richard Rider, has been floating around for years as a potential addition to the franchise. We haven't seen him yet, but if the films continue to draw on the events of "Annihilation," the fact that the Corps is already established makes it possible for the films to recreate one of the comic's biggest moments. As the opening shot in his war against the rest of the galaxy, Annihilus, well, annihilates the Nova Corps on the planet Xandar, leaving Rider as the sole survivor. Rich does eventually get his revenge, literally punching down Annihilus' throat and tearing out his guts in one of the most truly badass moments in Marvel Comics history, and one that plenty of fans would love to see recreated in the films.

Of course, insectoid space dictators and comic books being what they are, Annihilus did eventually make his way back from the dead, but that could be very beneficial considering that unlike the comics, the movies have a tendency to kill off their villains. Giving them the ability to return and rise again allows their characters to develop over time alongside the heroes, even if some of them definitely deserve their fate.

#3573. Alan Ritchson’s DC Future Just Got Murkier After James Gunn’s Sudden Exit

Following the announcement of James Gunn and Peter Safran stepping down as co-CEOs of DC Studios, Alan Ritchson's future in the DCU just got murkier. Just weeks ago, Safran confirmed that DC was in talks with Ritchson for multiple projects. Now that DC Studios will be under new leadership from former Marvel Studios executive Jeremy Latcham, these recent developments make Ritchson's role in the DCU much less clear. Given Ritchson's interest in joining the modern DCU, this sudden change certainly shakes his candidacy up.

Ritchson has appeared in several previous DCU projects in the past, including his role as Arthur Curry/Aquaman in the hit television series Smallville and Hank Hall/Hawk in the HBO Max series Titans. Ritchson's star power has grown immensely as the titular lead in Prime Video's massively successful Reacher franchise, suggesting that a more significant role would become available to him within Gunn and Safran's DCU. Now that Latcham, who served as a producer on The Avengers, Guardians of the Galaxy, and Spider-Man: Homecoming, is officially in the DCU driver's seat as of December 1, a completely new rollout strategy may be introduced that could exclude Ritchson.

During Gunn and Safran's 4-year run as CEOs and chairmen of DC Studios, they released a Superman reboot that introduced David Corenswet as the latest Man of Steel, as well as Supergirl, which fell far below box office expectations. The duo was expected to retain their executive roles after the historic Paramount/Skydance acquisition of Warner Bros. earlier this year, with their upcoming Superman sequel Man of Tomorrow as well as the long-awaited sequel to Robert Pattinson's Batman slated for release. While these projects remain intact, this leadership update has cast a cloud of uncertainty over the modern DCU, which includes how Ritchson could enter the fold.

Ritchson previously expressed interest in becoming the DCU's new Bruce Wayne/Batman, but talks with Gunn have led the 43-year-old actor to officially shut down that prospect. Instead, Gunn and Safran were searching for a role within their DCU that better fit Ritchson's age range, while also trying to land on a role that would have given Ritchson a more morally complex, less full-blown superhero character to play. It's important to note that Gunn and Safran are staying on at DC Studios to commit full-time to creative projects, suggesting that there is still hope for Ritchson to match their initial vision. If that happens, they'll have to do so under the discretion of Jeremy Latcham​​​​​.

On October 26, 2026, Peter Safran confirmed that DC was still in talks with Ritchson and noted that while interest was there, the right role for him had yet to be ascertained within Gunn's superhero universe. He stated, "We talked about a couple things, but nothing that's come to fruition at this point. I think he's great. Yeah, but he's just good. I also think there's a lot more depth to him than you might have seen. I think there's more that he can do that people haven't seen." These comments suggest that Safran and Gunn saw clear potential in the idea of Ritchson joining their DCU, specifically in finding him an ideal role that would tap into his abilities as both an action star and a performer.

Anthony Mackie faces a career criminal in Apple TV’s new 8-part heist thriller, combining a high-stakes vault robbery with an international chase.

The fact that Safran and Gunn hadn't landed on the right role for Ritchson in their DCU might actually work in Ritchson's favor, as Latcham may potentially be more eager to cash in on Ritchson's immediate draw and emergence as a one-man-army movie star. Ritchson remains one of the most sought-after leads in the action genre, having recently starred in Runner, War Machine, Playdate, and Motor City, all of which were met with mixed, if not poor, reviews. While the new leadership at DC Studios makes Alan Ritchson's DCU future unclear, it could also finally land him the role we've all been waiting for.

#3572. One of the Best QLED TVs of 2026 Is Over $1,300 Off Right Now

TCL has been pushing the boundaries of QLED TVs, making some of the best in the market at very competitive prices. This year, the company released its QM8L model, introducing a new design and impressive features and specs to a series that isn't even their flagship. Right now, the 65-inch QM8L is $1,197.99 (originally $2,499.99), $100 cheaper than it was just earlier this month, reaching its lowest price since it launched in April, according to price-tracking tools. Larger sizes are also seeing substantial discounts.

One of the first things you'll notice about the QM8L is the “Zero Border” bezel design, which gives it a modern, minimalistic look. When you turn it on, you'll likely note how bright this TV gets, which is a huge advantage QLEDs have over OLEDs. TCL claims it reaches 6,000 nits—seeing as the brightest OLED TV on the market only reaches 700 nits, no OLED can come close to this unit's brightness. Another important spec to note here is the local dimming zones: TCL claims this TV has up to 4,000, which means it gets top-tier backlight control, limited light blooming (thanks in part to TCL's "Halo Control"), and incredible contrast levels that some might not be able to distinguish from an OLED.

As many of us won't manually calibrate our TVs, the picture modes you can switch to in the settings will be most people's go-to. This TV's "Filmmaker mode" provides accurate color and picture, and if you're a gamer, you can use the native 144Hz high-refresh rate. If you don't already have a surround sound system at home and want to keep a minimalist setup, the QM8L comes with Dolby Atmos-ready Bang & Olufsen speakers, which offer above-average audio output compared to most TVs. You can read more about these features in CNET's 8.8/10 review. If 65 inches isn't quite right for your home theater setup, take a look at the QM8L's other sizes, which are also discounted right now.
